name: What is the best way to compare custom kitchen estimates from different contractors?

mainEntity.name: What is the best way to compare custom kitchen estimates from different contractors?
mainEntity.text: What is the best way to compare custom kitchen estimates from different contractors?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best way to compare custom kitchen estimates is to normalize the scope before looking at the bottom line. Two bids can look very different in price because one includes permits, demolition, structural work, and finish carpentry while another leaves those items out. Homeowners should compare cabinetry specs, countertop allowances, appliance assumptions, lighting scope, plumbing and electrical work, site protection, trash removal, and warranty terms. It also helps to check whether the estimate is based on actual selections or placeholder allowances, because a low allowance can make a proposal look cheaper than it really is. In custom work, the quality of detail matters as much as the total cost. A good estimate should make clear what happens if products change or hidden conditions are discovered. If one contractor is significantly lower than the others, ask whether important items were omitted. The most accurate estimate is not necessarily the lowest one; it is the one that most clearly defines the work.
acceptedAnswer.description: Compare estimates by scope, not just total price. The most useful bids show cabinetry details, finish allowances, labor, permits, exclusions, and change-order terms so you can see whether two proposals are actually covering the same work.
